newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan bills on Finance Ministry reforms finalised.
newsitem.headline: Japan bills on Finance Ministry reforms finalised.

text.p: The government on Monday finalised bills that would deprive the powerful Finance Ministry of its authority to inspect and supervise financial firms and bestow that role on a new agency, a government official said.
The legislation is expected to be approved at a cabinet meeting on Tuesday before being sent to the current session of parliament.
The reforms are expected to be implemented sometime between April 1, 1998, and July 1, 1998.
The bills are largely in line with a pact reached last December by the ruling LDP and the two parties with which it is loosely allied.
The main points of the bills are as follows:
-- A fully independent body would be established under the Prime Minister's Office to take over the ministry's functions of inspecting and supervising financial institutions.

-- The new agency would have the power to order a financial institution to halt business or to revoke its licence but would have to consult with the Finance Ministry if such actions would have a major impact on the financial system.

-- The new body would oversee all financial institutions -- banks, agricultural financial firms, non-bank financial firms, brokerage firms, labour credit associations -- which are currently supervised by different ministries. But it would share responsibility for inspecting and supervising institutions currently overseen by the Agriculture, Labour Trade ministries with the respective ministries.

-- The head of the agency would be appointed by the prime minister and have the right to appoint agency employees. The independence of the head of the agency and the employees must be strictly enforced.
-- The new body must hold regular meetings with the Finance Ministry to discuss financial matters from the viewpoint of maintaining Japan's credit order.
-- The Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC) will move from the purview of the Finance Ministry to that of the new body.
